In mathematics, '''Wilson polynomials''' are a family of [[orthogonal polynomials]] introduced by James Wilson<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wilson |first=James A. |date=July 1980 |title=Some Hypergeometric Orthogonal Polynomials |url=http://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/0511064 |journal=SIAM Journal on Mathematical Analysis |language=en |volume=11 |issue=4 |pages=690–701 |doi=10.1137/0511064 |issn=0036-1410|url-access=subscription }}</ref> that generalize [[Jacobi polynomials]], [[Hahn polynomials]], and [[Charlier polynomials]]. 

They are defined in terms of the [[generalized hypergeometric function]] and the [[Pochhammer symbol]]s by
:<math>p_n(t^2)=(a+b)_n(a+c)_n(a+d)_n {}_4F_3\left( \begin{matrix} -n&a+b+c+d+n-1&a-t&a+t \\ a+b&a+c&a+d \end{matrix} ;1\right).</math>

==See also==
*[[Askey–Wilson polynomial]]s are a q-analogue of Wilson polynomials.
